content:
The first iOS 27 public beta is now available for download on iPhone. Users can be among the first to experience Apple's most important software update of the year.

Siri AI is the headline feature this time. The new version also completely revamps the Screen Time experience, improves Liquid Glass, boosts performance, and includes many refinements to everyday use.

Below are instructions on how to install the beta, an overview of the new features, and which features are most worth trying first.

Table of Contents

  • How to join the iOS 27 public beta
  • Siri AI is the most important feature in iOS 27
  • Apple Intelligence expands to more iPhone apps
  • iOS 27 makes Liquid Glass more personal
  • iOS 27 is snappier, even on older devices
  • Major revamp for Screen Time and child safety features
  • More iOS 27 public beta features to explore
  • 9to5Mac Opinion
  • Get the most out of your Apple products

The Apple Beta Software Program is free and does not require a developer account.

Before getting started, back up your iPhone using iCloud or a computer. Beta software may contain bugs, reduce battery life, and cause compatibility issues with third-party apps.

The steps to join and install the beta are as follows:

  • Go to the Apple Beta Software Program website and choose "Sign Up" or "Sign In".
  • Sign in with the Apple Account on your iPhone, then accept the program terms and register your account.
  • Open the "Settings" app on your iPhone.
  • Go to "General" > "Software Update" > "Beta Updates".
  • Select "iOS 27 Public Beta".
  • Return to the "Software Update" screen, and when the beta appears, tap "Update Now".

Apple recommends installing beta software on a secondary device. If you use your main iPhone, be sure to make a recent backup first.

iOS 27 supports all iPhones that run iOS 26 — that is, iPhone 11 and later, as well as iPhone SE (second generation or later).

However, Apple Intelligence requires an iPhone 15 Pro or newer. Apple's newest on-device flagship models are supported on even fewer devices, but Siri AI only requires Apple Intelligence compatibility to work.

After installing the iOS 27 public beta, Siri AI is the feature most worth trying first.

Apple has rebuilt Siri from the ground up using its next-generation Apple Intelligence system. The assistant can now sustain conversations and search your personal information; it can also understand what's on screen, perform actions within apps, and answer a wider range of questions.

Siri's responses appear in the Dynamic Island. Pull the response down to open the full conversation. At the same time, a dedicated Siri app centralises your history and synchronises it via iCloud with privacy protection.

After installing the public beta, you can ask Siri to find specific details in Mail, Messages, Notes, Reminders, or Calendar. After that, you no longer need to repeat the original context — just ask follow-up questions directly. In iOS 27 beta 3, Siri can also begin to read information from some third-party apps.

The Camera app now includes a Visual Intelligence-enhanced Siri mode. For example, you can take a picture of a membership code and turn it into a Wallet pass; Siri can also import event details from a flyer.

In addition, Apple has added options to control Siri's speaking speed and expressiveness, found under "Settings" > "Siri" > "Voice". These settings also affect voice output in Maps and Safari.

Siri AI will initially only support selected English-speaking regions and will not be immediately launched in the EU. An Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone is also required. Some advanced on-device features require an iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max, or iPhone Air.

The iOS 27 public beta extends some of the most impressive AI features beyond Siri.

Safari can automatically organise tabs by topic, group bookmarks and Reading List items, and recommend recently closed topics on the start page. In addition, "Notify Me" can monitor web pages for changes, such as products coming back in stock. Safari can also create dedicated extensions based on natural language descriptions.

The Photos app adds three powerful editing tools: "Clean Up" can handle larger and more complex distractions; "Extend" can generate content outside the original frame; and "Spatial Recompose" lets you adjust the camera's angle and perspective after the shot has been taken.

Try using "Extend" on a photo where the horizon isn't straight; then use "Spatial Recompose" to recompose a poorly framed portrait.

The Passwords app can automatically replace eligible passwords that are weak or have been compromised, handle verification codes, and show progress via Live Activities. Shortcuts can now build automations from simple natural language instructions, and you can keep refining results through successive text-based edits.

Other new Apple Intelligence features include:

  • "Call Context" in the Phone app will display details such as reservation numbers when you call a business.
  • Image Playground gains photorealistic generation and natural language editing.
  • Calendar can create and edit events through natural language.

iOS 27 does not replace last year's Liquid Glass design — instead, it focuses on improving clarity and flexibility.

Controls can now more effectively fade out complex background content, while deeper edges and brighter highlights deliver greater layering, making buttons and text easier to read. App icons also feel richer in depth and dimension.

The first feature worth trying is the new Liquid Glass personalisation slider, found under "Settings" > "Display & Brightness". The slider ranges from fully transparent to fully tinted and applies to both iOS and third-party apps.

The iOS 27 speed improvements Apple promised aren't limited to the latest hardware. The company says app launches can be up to 30% faster; nearby AirDrop transfers up to 80% faster; and newly captured content can appear in the Photos app up to 70% faster.

Apple has extended CPU scheduling optimisations to iPhone 11. Unlocking, Home screen navigation, Control Centre scrolling, and Lock Screen transitions are all smoother; and the Camera opens faster in Low Power Mode.

iOS 27 also switches more intelligently between Wi-Fi and mobile data, so your iPhone is less likely to cling to a weaker signal when you leave home. Apple has also rebuilt Spotlight, Photos, and Mail search from the ground up; Mail can now show up to five ranked "Top Results".

iOS 27 brings major changes to Screen Time and parental controls. The new dashboard gives parents a clearer view of their child's activity and offers one-tap permission changes.

"App Limits" can now set restrictions for categories such as Games, Entertainment, and Social Media; "Schedules" can control which apps are usable during different periods. Parents can set separate routines for school days, after school, and weekends.

"Ask to Browse" extends the familiar "Ask to Buy" flow to websites. Children also need approval before adding new contacts. "Communication Safety" already detects and blurs nudity; in iOS 27, it will also step in when gory or violent content is detected.

One important note: the redesigned experience requires every device in the Family Sharing group to be running the OS 27 series.

These smaller changes below add up to a significant improvement:

  • "Messages" can keep uploading large media files in the background without blocking new messages afterwards; it also consolidates Tapback notifications in group chats.
  • "Photos" adds full-resolution Shared Albums, contributions from Windows and Android, keywords, star ratings, and custom slideshow playback.
  • You can save any frame from a video as a still photo with one tap.
  • Alarm volume can be adjusted independently of system volume.
  • Extra-large widgets can fill an entire Home Screen page.
  • AirPods gain a custom equaliser with adjustable bass, mid, and treble.
  • iPhone can connect directly to GymKit-enabled equipment.
  • FaceTime supports simultaneous front and rear camera recording on iPhone Air and iPhone 17 models.
  • The Home app gains more reliable HomeKit Secure Video and supports native 4K cameras via qualified hardware and iCloud+.

The iOS 27 public beta will be updated throughout the summer, with Apple planning to release the final version this autumn. If you encounter problems, you can use the built-in "Feedback Assistant" app to report them directly to Apple.

9to5Mac Opinion

iOS 27 is a remarkably strong update. At this point in summer, most iOS betas still have plenty of rough edges. While iOS 27 isn't perfect, it already delivers a noticeably smoother upgrade experience than iOS 26.

I really like the new Liquid Glass slider. I tried the most transparent setting (pulled all the way to the left), expecting to enjoy that dramatic effect, but I actually found the least transparent version (pulled all the way to the right) suits my taste best — it looks more comfortable and doesn't feel dated.

I've been using a Mac since Mac OS X Leopard, then quickly upgraded to Snow Leopard, and spent the most time on OS X Lion and Mountain Lion. I never truly used the Mac's Aqua interface, but the new Liquid Glass style (pulled all the way to the right) feels a bit like a modernised iOS version of Aqua.

Siri AI is clearly a winner: it's fast, capable, and visually and vocally strong — overall it brings Apple up to par with market expectations for AI. I personally still follow the day-to-day progress of the major AI labs closely, but I don't expect Apple to change Siri at breakneck speed. The benchmark Siri AI sets in iOS 27 is already solid.

Overall, iOS 27 is indeed an eagerly awaited update in terms of performance, stability, and making your iPhone more pleasant to use.
